utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Let me again interrupt. Again, you ask that this page be put away, Madam Vidovic, without you tendering it. I don't know whether you don't want to tender it or what, this page 127.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that page is part of the exhibit that has already been tendered earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, Madam Vidovic. The page that we admitted into evidence is page 139, full stop. So if you want this one in evidence, then you must get it tendered. You must tender it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You do tender. The page 127 of the B/C/S and 3 of the English translation is admitted into evidence. May it please be admitted and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become 1180.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry. Your Honour, I believe we also need the preceding page because that indicated the -- the paragraph that starts on this page actually began on the previous page. I just want to be clear that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- we're admitting two pages in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The English version will be page 2 and 3. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3 and 4 in the English, Your Honour, 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't it 2 and 3, Madam Vidovic? It's where it started on the previous page, not on the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the last sentence, if you'll recall, was on page 3 of the English version, and then it continued on to page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I would now like to ask you something, a very brief comment on your part. How did the civilian authorities function at the time when you were at the head of the TO Staff in Travnik, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: They were operational, in the sense that there was logistical support of the Territorial Defence, in terms of provisions, mobilisation, assistance in a accommodating refugees, and so on. They functioned, in principle, depending on the election results, so that certain parties, depending on the number of votes they got, split certain functions amongst them in the municipality; for example, the SDA party, as far as the defence section is concerned, appointed the TO Staff commander, and the HDZ was given the post of secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence of the Travnik Municipality. So these were these divisions, in terms of the results of the election results in the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the relationship of the civilian authorities was towards the armed forces? What was the relationship?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Because they held these very important segments, they imposed their own cadre, solutions, in terms of the defence, and I was appointed by the president of the Travnik Municipality, who was a member of the SDA party, so that they actually influenced cadre decisions because they had these key segments that they held on which the army mobilisation, logistics, provisions, and supplies depended on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But I would just like you to speak a little bit slower when you're answering. Now I would like to ask you this: You mentioned mobilisation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not understood what is the Secretariat of National Defence of the Municipality of Travnik. Could you please explain this, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. The Secretariat for the National Defence of the Municipality of Travnik was a civilian organ that dealt with the matters of recruitment, mobilisation, military record-keeping, military conscripts, so that they were in charge of entering conscripts into the military records by law, having their medical examinations, recruitments, sending them to serve mandatory military terms, and then they were deployed to the reserve compositions after serving their term of duty. So it was a civilian organ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you also explain what was the relationship between the Territorial Defence and this organ which you have spoken about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a professional organ from the beginning until the end, and the fact that we depended on the Secretariat and that it had responsibilities vis a vis us was something that they were actually carrying out, as far as they were able to do that in that situation. They were fulfilling their obligations towards the TO Staff as much as they could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the Territorial Defence depended from the Secretariat of the National Defence of the Municipality of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely, because they were in charge of mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Lattanzi.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, I was about to put these questions to you, Mr. Ribo, and so I would just like to then carry on from there. You answered that the Territorial Defence depended, in terms of logistics and mobilisation, from the Secretariat for National Defence. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next thing I want to ask you is: When we're talking about the subordination relationship, what was that relationship? Was the TO in any functional connection with this civilian body or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: We were in the functional connection as part of the system of command and control, under the TO Regional Staff in Zenica. So they were superior -- they were a superior command to me, and I was responsible to them. This part was actually that functional link. They had obligations towards us, of course. We also requested certain things from them, to occupy buildings for us, to provide material and equipment for us, because it was not something we could get for ourselves on the street or in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. So the National Defence Secretariat, you said, as a civilian body, controlled logistics and mobilisation. Because of that, what was its relationship? Did it have any particular kind of relationship towards the TO, in terms of cadre, appointments, and so on?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: They did not have anything to do with logistics. They were in charge of mobilisation. Thus, they were not obliged, in that sense, towards us, other than in terms of mobilisation. They were not entrusted with cadre appointments in the TO Staff because this was a civilian authority, when we're talking about the commander, and the commander would actually deal with his own subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you described a situation whereby the SDA appointed you and not the TO from Zenica. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. My appointment came from the chief of the Travnik Municipality, as a civilian body, a civilian organ, and not from the superior command of mine from Zenica, because these were like that. We were connected because of financing and supplies for Travnik. We were connected to the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And was this correct, in military soldierly terms, this thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to ask you to tell us briefly the TO Staff units.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: The TO Staff units included the following: The regional Staff in Turbe, the one in Travnik and Krpeljic, all these were regional staffs, the one in Han Bila, in Mehuric, the 1st and 2nd Travnik Detachments, the Karaula TO Detachment, the Staff TO Command, the Communications Platoon, the Military Police Platoon, and the Staff Security Protection and the 133-Millimetre Mortar Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, you've already said that in the course in 1992 and 1993, there were no weapons. Can you please briefly describe the situation, in terms of communication?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I have to tell you that it was also very difficult, the situation, what the Serbs and the former JNA did. They made a mistake in Croatia. They handed over the buildings and the communication systems without destroying them first, so they did not make the same mistake in Bosnia and Herzegovina. When we're talking about Bosnia and Herzegovina, what was the priority objective of the Serbs and the Yugoslav People's Army was to occupy the radio relay facilities, like Kozara, Vlasic, the transmitter that was in my territory, the territory of my municipality, Hum near Sarajevo, the main post office in Sarajevo and the one in Trebevic, and so on and so forth. So these were seized. They were confiscated by the Bosnian Serb Army and the JNA, and what was left to us as the only solution was to maintain Ham radio communications, to use those that were quite unreliable for the command-and-control system. Particularly, what was a problem was that the few communications systems that were there were of different types. They were not complimentary in order to be able to have good communications with the subordinate units and the superior command, and this made the command-and-control system very difficult. Sometimes, the units that were out in the field were left to themselves to make their own decisions and to command as well as they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1992 and 1993, were you able to communicate with Sarajevo or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: We, in Travnik, could not communicate with them. It was only toward the end of the year that, with great difficulty, we -- these municipalities that were almost fully surrounded used courier communication and had great difficulties in arriving at the information out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it came to Sarajevo, did you use courier communication?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No. We used it only as far as the Zenica Regional TO Staff. We couldn't use that type of communication as far as Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your evidence, you said that the HDZ founded the HVO. Can you tell us what sort of impact it had on the situation in the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: At the very outset, we were faced with certain difficulties with regard to the military structure that refused to place themselves under our command. They set up a number of check-points which made difficult the circulation of individuals from different municipalities and regions. It was at these check-points that they exercised violence and made the general situation in Central Bosnia very difficult. At one point, the policemen of Tihomir Blaskic, as the commander of Travnik -- or rather, it was his neighbouring commander because he was the commander in Vitez. They disarmed me, and I tried to get my weapons back through nonviolent means. It was these units and their check-points that made our movement difficult even towards our defence lines. Our units would be stopped on their way, their weapons would be taken off them, and they had to work to get their weapons back. And all of this made the situation very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I appeal to you to shorten your answers and to speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown document D905. For the record, this is a report on the situation in the Novi Travnik Municipality, dated the 19th of October, 1992. I want to direct your attention to the last and penultimate paragraphs of the document. Could you please enlarge the Bosnian version as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I know that you can't be very familiar with the document, but please read the last two paragraphs because you might have some knowledge of the situation described here. It is stated here that: "The Zenica Region Army Staff constantly insisted on negotiations with our command, which we have refused because we have no direct links with our commander, Mr. Tihomir Blaskic; and Mr. Kordic did not allow any negotiations at the time and was currently in Novi Travnik. All the roads reading from Novi Travnik are blocked." This is my question for you: Does this document reflect the situation in October 1992, in terms of the relations between the HVO and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge of the attempts to negotiate with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Of course, I had knowledge of that. In the municipality's neighbouring to ours, like the Zenica TO, they told us not to meddle into the conflict in Novi Travnik especially not with our units, and we honoured that order. We acted upon that order because we felt that it was the matter of the Zenica Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you try to avoid conflicts with Croats in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be given an exhibit number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number 1181.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have another document left. Can the witness be shown D906. For the record, this is an HVO document, order on further activities, dated the 22nd of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a rather short document, Mr. Ribo, which speaks of a request to strengthen the blockade on all the roads leading to Novi Travnik. Have a look at the document first. Does it reflect the balance of powers between the HVO and the TO in October of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept, Your Honour. I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, can you comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Of course, I can. This is a document issued by Commander Milivoj Petkovic. In the -- among the addressees, you can see that these are the municipalities on the fringes of Central Bosnia, and it speaks of the full blockade of Central Bosnia. Nobody could get into Central Bosnia or get out of it without the knowledge and approval of the HVO. So there was a full blockade of Central Bosnia in place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be assigned an exhibit number. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number 1182.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe it is time for the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, let us move to a different topic now. At the start of your testimony, you said that the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina passed a decision to unite all the armed forces in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown D900.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document. While working as the commander of the TO Staff in Travnik, did you have occasion to see this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please direct your attention to the first three items of the document. I will quote only item 3, where it says: "All armed groups and individuals who fail to report and to place themselves under the command of the municipal Territorial Defence Staffs or the district Territorial Defence Staffs or the City of Sarajevo Territorial Defence Staff shall be classified as paramilitary formations and shall be sanctioned according to the Law." Can you just briefly, very briefly, explain to us what the meaning of this decision was in practice?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: In practice, it meant that all the units had to be placed under the command of the Territorial Defence since it was the only armed force; and, of course, everything that was set up outside of the Territorial Defence was deemed to be paramilitary.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did this decision define the hallmarks of such units?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This decision regulated that matter as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: By clearly stipulating what the Territorial Defence units would wear, in which territories they would be deployed, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, I'd like you to explore with the witness just which armed groups was this decision meant to cover. What were the armed groups that the president wanted to integrate? Of course, notably, did the decision cover the Mujahedin groups which might at that time have begun to enter the country?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please bear in mind the date of the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the top of the document to see the date -- or rather, it's at the bottom, the 9th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've heard the question put by His Honour. What sort of armed groups were subject to this decision?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: The Patriotic League, the Green Berets, the MUP loyal to Bosnia-Herzegovina, an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina. All that had to be placed under the single command of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard the question put by His Honour Judge Harhoff. Did this also apply to the Mujahedin, if they were already there at the time?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: The decision is dated the 9th of April, 1992. At that time, not even the fighting had practically broken out. I believe that in my area, the conflict broke out on the 22nd of April [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't answer the Judge's question. Were there Mujahedin in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you have no further questions in relation to this document, Your Honour, can this document be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction: The date was not the 22nd of April, but the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me. No, I have no further questions, except for the date. In the English version, down on the bottom, the date seems to be the 9th of April, and I had been unaware of this date when I put my question, my first question. But maybe just clarify which is the correct date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document states as, as the date, the 9th of April, 1992, and that's what the witness said. I don't know what's in the transcript. The 9th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what did you say? When did the conflicts break out in your area?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: In the area of Turbe, the conflict broke out on the 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I believe we've cleared this up now. Can the document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1183.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put the document away now, and can the witness be shown Exhibit 116. This document does not have an English version. What matters is the photograph only. Can you please show the images on the screen only. These are insignia. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the earlier document, if you'll recall, mentioned insignia and ranks, and stated that different groups were active under different insignia. Do you recall that bit from the earlier document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which of the insignia that we can see here, if any, have to do with the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: When it comes to the Territorial Defence, it's the insignia number 7. That was the insignia we wore on our right arm.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the insignia under number 12, what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: It refers to the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, when the armija was formed. When the TO became the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina this was its insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain the insignia under number 4?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: This is the insignia of the MUP, the reserve and the active MUP forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you know, can you please explain what is under number 1? What is this insignia?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: That is insignia of the MOS.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is that MOS?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Those are the Muslimanske Snage, Muslim Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the beginning of your testimony, you said that there was resistance for the armed groups in the area of Travnik to report to the Staff, and we saw this decision from April, I think the 9th of April, 1992, ordering the unification of all the armed groups into the Territorial Defence. I want to ask you this: After the 9th of April, 1992, was the forming of groups and units outside of the TO stopped? Did that cease, according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And why was this? Can you describe that a bit?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: For the simple reason that certain groups, like the Patriotic League and the Green Berets, did not wish to place themselves under the control of the TO. They acted on their own initiative, and then certain religious circles did not agree with the composition and the command and control and activities of the TO Staff. So they also initiated the formation of the Muslim Armed Forces in analogy to the HVO and the HOS.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the attitude of the religious circles towards the Territorial Defence? Do you have any examples that could illustrate this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may respond. Your Honours, I will rephrase the question. If it was prompting speculation, I will phrase it differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you were the Staff commander of the Territorial Defence. Did you, in this function of yours, have any contacts or any experiences with the religious circles?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you have any experience when we're talking about the area or the territory used by your units or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Where my first Travnik detachment was located, it's the Travnik Medresa religious facility now. Before the former Yugoslavia, it was a religious facility. Then the authorities of Yugoslavia confiscated it from the Islamic religious community, and it was used as a furniture sales outlet in the former Yugoslavia. Then at the beginning of the war, I located the 1st Travnik Detachment there, and Efendi Avdibegovic, Nusrit Avdibegovic, the Travnik Mufti, asked through this commander for this unit to move out because this was a religious facility. Then after consultations, the commander moved out of this building. We left it and simply handed it over to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that they did not allow you to use their facility?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Of course. They insisted, for their own purposes and objectives, that we leave and abandon that facility, which is what we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned earlier that the religious leaders supported the establishment of the Muslim Armed Forces in Travnik. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber who these religious leaders were in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Primarily, it is the Travnik Mufti, Nusret Avdibegovic, and then Ahmed Adilovic, who had a Master's degree; and these were the two persons in the Travnik Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were talking about Efendi Nusret Avdibegovic and then Ahmed Adilovic; is that correct? I'm doing this for the transcript: Nusret Avdibegovic and Ahmed Adilovic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, again: Was there any reason or not because of which the religious circles did not wish to support the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. There was, in the sense that they considered us to be less a Muslim than we actually were, and they didn't trust the TO Staff that was multi-ethnic, as I explained in the document of the list of the employees of the TO Staff. They automatically did not trust the Staff because of this multi-ethnic aspect because they believed that it should all be a single ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you this: Would it be wrong or not to believe that the MOS, the Muslim Armed Forces, was an integral part of the TO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the status of the Muslim Armed Forces, if you know, and was there a relationship between them and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: The Muslim Armed Forces were independent units outside of the system of control of the Travnik Staff, so they were not part of my forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "part of my forces," what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Units of the Travnik Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now look at document D52, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Madam Vidovic. I thought you were about to leave this document; and so before we leave it, I would like to put some questions to the witness because some of the insignia are interesting in the perspective of this case. I think, by the way, we have seen this exhibit before. Now, Mr. Witness, insignia numbers 1, 19, and 22 seem to all relate to the Muslimanske Snage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the entire 19 and 22, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So if this is correct, Mr. Ribo, are these, then, the insignia that were sported by the members of the Muslim Forces that you just spoke about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only insignia number 1. That is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, the colours are different, but I know that it was actually the black colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So the soldiers who were wearing this black insignia, as displayed in example number 1, they were outside the TO, you just told us. So under whose command were these Muslimanske Snage then operating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were supported by the religious circles, and they acted independently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I am not quite sure if at the point you are -- the point of time of which you are speaking. Was that before or after the establishment of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the establishment of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. While I was the commander, they operated independently. They were not under my command. They were more posers, and they continued with such activities after, when the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established; but, again, they were independent because of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. An order was issued, I think, in September sometime that armija units should be formed, and the corps were formed on the 1st of December, then brigades were formed, and then they disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. So what you are telling us is that the Muslimanske Snage were incorporated into the ABiH brigades later on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please tell us, then, how it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The Muslim Armed Forces, their members, when the MOS was dismantled in Travnik and brigades were formed, some individual soldiers became part of some brigades. They joined some brigades, such as the 7th Muslim, 312th, 306th, 307th, 325th. So, depending on from which area they came when the Travnik MOS was disbanded, they went and joined those units, not as a complete unit of the Muslim Armed Forces. That was not, as such, incorporated into the army force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just to be clear, does this mean that after the establishment of the brigades, the new brigades under the new Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina after September 1992, the Muslim Forces ceased to exist as independent units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The MOS in Travnik ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I want you to look at example number 15. Do you recognise this insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I then also wanted you to have a look at the last insignia, number 24; and my question is, again, if you recognise this insignia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't recognize this insignia either. I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Ribo, if you could have a look at example number 17.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw this insignia on any member, no, in the territory of the Travnik Municipality; and even later, really, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, very brief. When did the Muslim Armed Forces, as they were fighting under this number 1 insignia, when were they established, created, more or less, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say that this was sometime in May 1992, May or June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, they will have existed from May to September, if I have understood you rightly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence -- I beg your pardon. It's an exhibit already.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question relating to the Muslim Forces. What you said, in respect of the continuation and how long they were operative in September 1992, you're talking about the Travnik region; is that how we can understand that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, the Travnik region.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know about other regions?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, we can put this document away, and the witness can now look at D52, D52. For the transcript, this an overview of the Staffs and TO units under the Travnik TO in May 1992, the 23rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ribo, I would like you to look at this document page by page. First of all, do you agree that, during proofing, I showed you this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. And did you look at it carefully?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we now look at page 2 in both versions, the next page. English version as well. The next page, then, and the following page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does this document show?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I didn't get the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the last page, please. The last page of the Bosnian version, please, if possible. Maybe we can resolve the problem at this point if we show the witness the entire document on the ELMO. Perhaps you can just show it to my learned friend from the Prosecution before the witness sees the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought we were putting it on the ELMO. I think counsel said to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the last page now?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know this document from before?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said, a moment ago, that it showed the composition of the Staff of the Territorial Defence in Travnik. Is that right? Having reviewed this document, did you see if there were any Muslim Armed Forces as part of the Staff or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Since this is my document, which was sent to the Staff in Sarajevo, I can tell you that it clearly shows that there are no Muslim Armed Forces, nor were any ever part of my force. Had there been any, I would have indicated them here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can this document be assigned an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, I just want to understand what each column is telling us; otherwise, it doesn't mean much to me, and I don't even know how to determine that the Muslims were not part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bear with me for a moment. Can we go back to page 1 of the document of the English version. The document will -- rather, the witness will have the Bosnian version over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In column number 1, we have a number, is that right, then we have the Staff or rather, the unit? We have the title of the Staff or the unit concerned, and then the number of officers and soldiers and the area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Vidovic. Can the witness explain that, rather than you explaining it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you do that, please?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I can. What we can see here is the composition and structure of the Staff of the Territorial Defence of Travnik by different columns. Under the heading "Staff Unit," we have the different units of the Territorial Defence; for instance, the zone or sector staff Turbe. And what is next mentioned are the units that are part of that Staff under numbers 1 through 10. Earlier on, I said which units were part of the Travnik TO Staff. The next column says "Manpower Levels."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you talk of the zone or sector staff Turbe, what are you referring to on this page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Witness, please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have in front of me what appears to be page 2, not the cover page. In the English version, you have the first page; whereas, I have page 2 in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we have the same page for both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us take as an example the zone or sector staff Travnik, which is in the bottom part of the table; and there, under ordinal numbers 1 through 11, you have the subordinated units listed belong to the zone or sector staff Travnik. Whatever was part of the Travnik zone or sector staff was listed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand you. I don't understand you. First of all, I'd like to go slow. Tell us what number 1 means, tell us what "Staff Unit" means, tell us what "enlistment" or "officer" means, tell us what "non-commissioned officer" means, tell us about "soldiers" means, "total" and "disposition," and then we can understand that line. Then you can tell us how you now come to the conclusion that all this page belongs to the Travnik zone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us take column -- or rather, let us take row 1, or rather, you want columns. Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Row 1, row 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Column 1, it says: "Municipal TO Staff, Travnik." That's my command. At the time when I wrote this report to the Ministry of Defence in Sarajevo, I placed the heading "Enlistment" or "Manpower Levels," which meant that I had 22 officers, one non-commissioned officer, and one soldier. The Staff, my command, had 24 men in total. The TO Staff was stationed at the feature called "Plava Voda" in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we just determine one thing. How, by looking at that row, do you determine that there are no Muslim people in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The ethnic makeup was not sought here. What we were looking for is the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it is not correct, what you said earlier, that by looking at this document, we can see that it did not have any Muslims in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there must have been an error. I spoke of the MOS unit being or not being part of my structure, and not of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Now, how do we determine, by looking at that row, that none of those 24 people is a member of MOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, simply because they were not part of my forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I'm trying to find the sentence that was mentioned because that's not how it was put. We were given the impression that by looking at this document, you can see that none of the people here is a member of the Muslimanske Snage. I want to find out, and that's why I asked the question. I don't know how to determine that none of these people is a member of the Muslimanske Snage, and that's why I stopped and asked these questions. Now, if anybody can find that sentence, I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I didn't make myself clear. The MOS and its members were not part of my forces, either as a unit or as individual members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I understand that that is your testimony. I'm saying we were referred to this document. We were told that by looking at this document, we can see that none of the people here is a MOS member. Now I want to see and I want to find out how we make that determination by looking at this document, not by listening to your testimony, but by looking at this document. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of assistance, please turn to page 72, line 14 of the transcript. My question was whether members of units of Muslimanske Snage were part of the TO, so I was referring to a unit and not to individual members. And the witness has been referring to a unit of the MOS and not to individuals, and that's what the witness was trying to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. At line 14, page 72, you said: "You said a moment ago that it showed the composition of the Staff of the Territorial Defence in Travnik; is that right? Having reviewed this document, did you see if there were any Muslim Armed Forces as part of the Staff or not?" Then the answer was: "Since this is my document, which was sent to the staff in Sarajevo, I can tell you that it clearly shows that there are no Muslim armed forces, nor were any ever part of my force. Had there been any, I would have indicated them here."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My problem is: What is it that is not here, which, if it had been here, would indicate that the Muslim armed forces were part of this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They would have had to be included in the list of units. The Muslim Armed Forces were units, and we're referring to units. Had they been part of my TO Staff, they would have been listed in column 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Am I to understand that you could not, for instance, have, if we look at row 3, you could not have a detachment TO in Karaula composed of MOS members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They would have to appear there as Muslimanske Snage; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic. Did you ask that the document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1184.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, in response to His Honour's question, you said that you knew that the Muslim Forces existed or were set up in the month of May of 1992. Did you try to obtain more information on these forces and their units?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I must admit that I did. I sought information from my assistant for security, Esad Sipic. I asked him that he provide me with information about what sort of Muslim units they were, who was leading them, and so on and so forth. I wanted to know what this was all about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive that sort of information?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I received information from my assistant for security to the effect that these were units set up under the wing of the Muslim religious community, that they were headed by an individual named "Kara," that they were billeted at the facility where my 1st Travnik Detachment was located, and that they were not armed. This was the case at the time when I was seeking this information, and it was on this basis that I had knowledge about what this was all about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, when you mentioned the individual who was leading them at the time, you mentioned a name. Can you please spell the name out?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: The commander -- or rather, at the head of these units, according to the information my assistant for security got, was an individual called "Tara," T-A-R-A.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who had put at their disposal this facility, since it was a facility, if I understood, which was of a TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Islamic community placed it at the disposal of the Muslim Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This facility wasn't under the control of the TO of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Initially, it was because my unit was billeted there. However, at the request of the Travnik Mufti, my battalion commander, with my approval, handed the facility over to the Muslim religious community because we believed, having been a religious facility, that it would be used for religious purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you report the information you got to your superior command?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit 118 at this time, please. Can we turn to page 2 of the document in both versions. For the record, this is an Official Note of the Staff of the Army of the Zenica District, dated the 1st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the number, please? What was the number of the document, please? We don't have it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 118. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this isn't a lengthy document. I believe you've read it, or do you need more time?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I can't see the lower part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the bottom of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document mentions the initials "RH." Are they your initials?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where are these initials? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, possibly in the English -- well, can you please scroll up the English version so that we can see the beginning of the text, the first sentence. Actually, it's the first line, the last two letters. I will quote the sentence: "On the 21st of July, 1992, I received the commander of the Municipal Staff in Travnik, RH, for an interview, upon his request, and he informed me of the following:"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, can you please explain if what is said in the document is correct, that you were summoned or invited to a meeting at the Zenica District Staff; and if you did, what was going on there? What did you report the Staff about, if you informed it about anything?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I was invited for a briefing by the commander of the TO Regional District Defence Staff; and after the briefing was completed, I gave a statement to this gentleman, Nasid, who was the assistant commander for security of the Zenica District Defence Staff. Of course, I gave him the insignia, together with this statement, the insignia of the Muslim Armed Forces in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what exactly did you inform him about?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I informed him on the basis of the information that I had through the security assistant, that in the region of my municipality, the Municipality of Travnik, Muslim Forces were being formed, led by a man named "Zihnija." It was a self-organised force exclusively on a mono-ethnic basis. They were giving each soldier 50 German marks each and were giving others 200 marks, to the officers, to join them. They were giving them weapons and food. They were simply trying to pull out people from the Territorial Defence and other forces, certain fighters, and attract others to them, especially refugees who had come from the Bosanska Krajina. I can say here that there were particularly people who joined the Muslim Armed Forces who were unfit for military duty, and they did not serve their mandatory military term of duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's stay on this document. Zihnija is the ideological leader that is being referred to here. Do you know anything about this person? Who was that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: The ideological leader mentioned here as Zihnija was not -- actually, the unit was supported by the Islamic religious circles, the Islamic religious functionaries. Zihnija Aganovic was the commander of the regional Patriotic League, and he supported the Mujahedin. So we must differentiate between the Muslim Armed Forces and the Mujahedin. The Muslim Armed Forces were supported by the Islamic circles, and the Mujahedins were supported by this certain Zihnija Aganovic, who was the commander of the Regional Staff of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because it is said here, in this document of yours, that Zihnija was the ideological leader of the Muslim Forces.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, it wasn't him. These were actually the Travnik Mufti, Avdibegovic and Ahmed Mufti. These were the ideological leaders of the Muslim Armed Forces of Travnik. Zihnija Aganovic was the one who supported the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, this is very important for all of us. Zihnija Aganovic, you said that it was a person who was at the head of the Patriotic League, the Regional Staff of the Patriotic League. What was his role, if he did have any political or military role later, in later events?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Besides being the commander of the Regional Staff of the Patriotic League, he was also very influential in the SDA party, but he was also for a time the president of the Travnik District.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, this Patriotic League that he headed, at the time when you were the TO Staff commander, in that period, did it ever join the TO Staff or not in that period?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another aspect of this document. You informed there or reported there that money was being given. You informed the Zenica District Defence Staff that money was being offered. Is that how it really was on the ground?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then it is said that there were rumours among the Muslim population that the Muslim Forces were the only ones to protect the Muslims. Were such rumours spread?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. These rumours were spread, and they were more and more intense and stronger as these Muslim Armed Forces began to be established. We had problems to keep our fighters in the TO because of these favourable conditions being offered, to stop them from going over. We had to inform our forces very well in order to prevent our members of the TO from switching to the Muslim Armed Forces. We were simply two enemies. We simply couldn't stand each other, the Muslim Armed Forces and the TO Staff. You saw why; because we were a multi-ethnic command, we were officers of the former JNA, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We can put this document away now, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can we scroll down the English version, please. Who's Nasid Agic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Agic, Nasid Agic, was deputy commander -- assistant commander for security of the commander of the Regional Staff of the TO in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if you look at - and I'm reading the English version and I don't know whether the B/C/S is similar - the last paragraph, it says: "In recent time, they are behaving aggressively towards the members of the OS. They are threatening them and taking away their weapons. Serbs and Croats from the TO Municipal Staff in Travnik are leaving the Staff because of the establishment of such a unit that is under the command of Travnik Staff." What is meant by "Travnik Staff" at the end of that sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were not under my command, and that is why I think that this sentence is not formulated correctly. I did not give such a statement. I wouldn't give a statement against the Muslim Forces had they been in my Staff. I'm not that crazy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking because that looks like a self-contradiction. Thank you for the explanation. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. You have spoken of the composition, mono-ethnical composition of that group of the Muslim Forces which were fighting under this insignia. Those were people who were only Bosnians and not foreigners? They were only from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only from Bosnia. MOS, the Muslim Armed Forces, were only people from Bosnia, according to the information that I have, so only from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other thing I wanted to know: You said, a while ago, that these Muslim Forces had been established during the month of May, but you were taking them only in July. Now, how did this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They were founded or established in May and they were growing gradually, so we didn't really attach much importance to these forces. Why did I intervene in respect of the District Staff? At the end of July, or in mid-July, I was at a meeting in the Travnik Municipality, at the War Presidency, where we discussed a joint command of the Travnik Municipality armed forces. This is when the Croats mentioned that they saw that there were some Mujahids of the MOS. And on the basis of that statement and my own information, I ordered the security -- assistant for security of the commander to find out more about these forces, who they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this document away now, and can the witness now look at Exhibit 55. This is a video clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, this clip shows some people. Do you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I know the Nusret Avdibegovic, the Travnik Mufti.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person you said supported the MOS?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, that is the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which person is he here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's to the left on the photograph that I see, with the white cap or hat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we continue with the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, first of all, is it correct that I showed you this footage during proofing?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us, do you know what this footage depicts? Do you know about this event that was videotaped?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: I know what it's about, but I don't know when it happened. I think that this was the celebration or the ceremony, the formal ceremony, of the formation of this force, the Muslim Armed Forces, and it is the oath-swearing ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you now is this: When this footage was made, you were the Staff commander of the TO. Who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought he said he doesn't know when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "I know what it's about, but I don't know when it happened." So he can't answer whether, when it happened, he was the Staff person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, you heard what the Judge said. Now, this is what I want to ask you: When you were the commander of the TO Staff, did people give an oath in front of you, before you, as the TO Staff commander?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No. They said their oath before my deputy, the most serious -- or senior representatives of my command. But, actually, in the majority of the cases, I was also there during the oath ceremony because it is the most formal of ceremonies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this footage that you see, that is, the formal oath-swearing ceremony, do you remember, were you the TO Staff commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you or any of your emissary attend this event?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the members of the Muslim Forces from the Travnik area swear their oath before you or anyone from your area?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is already an exhibit. I would like the witness to look at different video footage, and this is Exhibit number 84.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a technical problem, Your Honours. We apologise. Your Honours, we apologise. I didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just asking if Madam Gluhic perhaps needs assistance from the technicians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will come back to this video footage tomorrow, and now I'm going to show another exhibit to the witness. Then tomorrow, in the morning, we will show this video clip. Can the witness now look at Exhibit 103. For the transcript, it is the list of fighters of the Travnik Muslim Armed Forces of the Travnik area of the 15th of September, 1992. Can you scroll down the document, please, to the end. Scroll down the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, can you please look at the names on the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then look at the last page of this document now; also in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this, witness: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: During the testimony before this Tribunal in the Hadzihasanovic-Kubara case.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the capacity of the commander of the TO Staff in Travnik, did you ever receive this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No. I had never seen it before the Hadzihasanovic trial. There are some illogical elements in it which are not typical of my unit and Staff; for instance, the stamp. My subordinate units did not have stamps, and particularly not one such as this. Not a single subordinate unit had its own stamp; they all had the stamp of my own Staff. There is no logic in my subordinate unit having a stamp such as this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, whether having such a stamp is possible or not, is it possible, in September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: For my unit, no. I never received a list such as this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 1 once more. The English version is fine. Can we see the heading of the document and can it be enlarged? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the document reads: "Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Staff of the Armed Forces, Muslim Forces, Travnik," and next the reference number and date. How do you understand this, the Staff of the Armed Forces and then the Muslim forces in Travnik, all topped by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina? How do you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Well, they could have a heading telling whatever you wanted. There were different headings at the time. What is interesting is that where you have the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Staff of the Armed Forces, they don't mention Travnik at this stage. Another thing that is quite interesting is that it says: "State secret," and this is just a list of an odd number of persons. Next, where they say: "We're sending you a list of the fighters of the Muslim Forces in Travnik in our area," we don't know on whose request this is and why they're sending this list. Normally, in a document, there is always a reference back to a document, an order, or some other sort of a document in reference to which this is sent. Besides that, I would always have to refer to a unit that would find this list that I'm sending helpful.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We said that it says: "The Muslim Forces, Travnik." Can you tell us whether this document ever reached your TO Staff?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please look at the first name listed here: Adilovic, son of Becir, Ahmed. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: He's precisely one of the religious leaders from the Municipality of Travnik who set this unit up together with the support of the Travnik Mufti, Nusret Avdibegovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time of your term as commander of the TO Staff, was Adilovic ever your subordinate?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, never. He never came over to the Command, and I never spoke to him, although he comes from my native village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Name number 2 is Makteuf, Muhammad, Abdulah. Do you know who that individual is?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I know he lived in the Municipality of Travnik as a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina for some 15 years before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. I have one more question for you. Do you have any knowledge if there were any foreigners in the MOS in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge to that effect. They simply weren't getting along because of the practicing of religious beliefs. There were two different Islamic currents, I would say. But I know that there were no foreigners there in the MOS.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I would like to interrupt my examination at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. We'll then take an adjournment and come back tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of March, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
